## Administrations

### list

`administrations.list`

List the administrations the token can access, with id, name, currency and access level

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.administrations.list({});
```

**Input:** _empty object_


**Output:** `object[]`

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Output full type">

```ts
{
  id?: string | number | null,
  name?: string | null,
  language?: string | null,
  currency?: string | null,
  country?: string | null,
  time_zone?: string | null,
  access?: string | null,
  suspended?: boolean | null,
  period_locked_until?: string | null | null,
  period_start_date?: string | null
}[]
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


---

## Assets

### create

`assets.create`

Create a new asset (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.assets.create({
	asset: {
		name: 'Website Relaunch',
		ledger_account_id: '458026356994737217',
		purchase_date: '2026-04-09',
		purchase_value: '100.00',
	},
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `asset` | `object` | No | — |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="asset full type">

```ts
{
  name: string,
  ledger_account_id: string | number,
  purchase_date: string,
  purchase_value: string | number | null,
  value_change_plan_attributes?: {
    lifespan_in_years: string | number | null,
    residual_value?: string | number | null
  }
}
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `ledger_account_id` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `name` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `purchase_date` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `purchase_value` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | — |
| `calculated_purchase_value` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | — |
| `current_value` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | — |
| `value_change_plan` | `object \| null` | No | — |
| `disposal` | `object \| null` | No | — |
| `value_changes` | `object[] \| null` | No | — |
| `sources` | `object[] \| null` | No | — |
| `reinvestment_reserve_purchase` | `object \| null` | No | — |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="value_change_plan full type">

```ts
{
  lifespan_in_years?: number | null,
  residual_value?: string | number | null | null,
  active?: boolean | null,
  monthly_depreciation?: string | number | null | null
} | null | null
```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="disposal full type">

```ts
{
  date?: string | null,
  reason?: string | null,
  externally_booked?: boolean | null,
  asset_id?: string | number | null,
  reinvestment_reserve_sale?: {
    id?: string | number | null,
    amount?: string | number | null | null,
    date?: string | null,
    disposal_id?: string | number | null
  } | null | null
} | null | null
```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="value_changes full type">

```ts
{
  type?: string | null,
  date?: string | null,
  amount?: string | number | null | null,
  description?: string | null | null,
  externally_booked?: boolean | null,
  asset_id?: string | number | null
}[] | null
```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="sources full type">

```ts
{
  id?: string | number | null,
  asset_id?: string | number | null,
  detail_id?: string | number | null,
  general_journal_document_entry_id?: string | number | null
}[] | null
```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="reinvestment_reserve_purchase full type">

```ts
{
  id?: string | number | null,
  amount?: string | number | null | null,
  date?: string | null,
  asset_id?: string | number | null
} | null | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### delete

`assets.delete`

Delete an asset (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.assets.delete({ id: '458026356994737217' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Moneybird accepted the call; it answered with no body. |

### disposals.create

`assets.disposals.create`

Create a disposal (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.assets.disposals.create({ id: '458026356994737217', date: '2026-04-09', reason: 'out_of_use' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `date` | `string` | Yes | Has to be after the purchase date of the asset, and cannot be in the future or in the locked period of the administration. |
| `reason` | `out_of_use \| sold \| private_withdrawal \| divested` | Yes | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `date` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `reason` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `externally_booked` | `boolean \| null` | No | — |
| `asset_id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `reinvestment_reserve_sale` | `object \| null` | No | — |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="reinvestment_reserve_sale full type">

```ts
{
  id?: string | number | null,
  amount?: string | number | null | null,
  date?: string | null,
  disposal_id?: string | number | null
} | null | null
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### list

`assets.list`

List all assets, one page at a time (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.assets.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `ledger_account_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `active` | `boolean \| string` | No | Whether to include only active assets |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="items full type">

```ts
{
  id?: string | number | null | null,
  ledger_account_id?: string | number | null | null,
  name?: string | null,
  purchase_date?: string | null,
  purchase_value?: string | number | null | null,
  calculated_purchase_value?: string | number | null | null,
  current_value?: string | number | null | null,
  value_change_plan?: {
    lifespan_in_years?: number | null,
    residual_value?: string | number | null | null,
    active?: boolean | null,
    monthly_depreciation?: string | number | null | null
  } | null | null,
  disposal?: {
    date?: string | null,
    reason?: string | null,
    externally_booked?: boolean | null,
    asset_id?: string | number | null,
    reinvestment_reserve_sale?: {
      id?: string | number | null,
      amount?: string | number | null | null,
      date?: string | null,
      disposal_id?: string | number | null
    } | null | null
  } | null | null,
  value_changes?: {
    type?: string | null,
    date?: string | null,
    amount?: string | number | null | null,
    description?: string | null | null,
    externally_booked?: boolean | null,
    asset_id?: string | number | null
  }[] | null,
  sources?: {
    id?: string | number | null,
    asset_id?: string | number | null,
    detail_id?: string | number | null,
    general_journal_document_entry_id?: string | number | null
  }[] | null,
  reinvestment_reserve_purchase?: {
    id?: string | number | null,
    amount?: string | number | null | null,
    date?: string | null,
    asset_id?: string | number | null
  } | null | null
}[]
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### reinvestmentReservePurchase.create

`assets.reinvestmentReservePurchase.create`

Create a reinvestment reserve purchase: records that part of the asset's purchase value is funded from the reinvestment reserve ("herinvesteringsreserve") (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.assets.reinvestmentReservePurchase.create({ id: '458026356994737217', amount: '121.00' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `amount` | `string \| number \| null` | Yes | An amount of money. Both a decimal and a string '10,95' are accepted. A string is bound to the same range as a number, -1,000,000,000 &lt;= *n* &lt;= 1,000,000,000. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `amount` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | — |
| `date` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `asset_id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |



---


| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Moneybird accepted the call; it answered with no body. |

### valueChanges.createArbitrary

`assets.valueChanges.createArbitrary`

Create an arbitrary value change (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.assets.valueChanges.createArbitrary({
	id: '458026356994737217',
	date: '2026-04-09',
	amount: '121.00',
	description: 'Consulting April',
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `date` | `string` | Yes | Has to be after the purchase date of the asset, and cannot be in the future or in the locked period of the administration. |
| `amount` | `string \| number \| null` | Yes | An amount of money. Both a decimal and a string '10,95' are accepted. A string is bound to the same range as a number, -1,000,000,000 &lt;= *n* &lt;= 1,000,000,000. |
| `description` | `string` | Yes | — |
| `externally_booked` | `boolean` | No | Set to true if the value change is already externally booked and doesn't need to be booked by Moneybird. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `type` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `date` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `amount` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | — |
| `description` | `string \| null \| null` | No | — |
| `externally_booked` | `boolean \| null` | No | — |
| `asset_id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |

### additionalCharges.create

`contacts.additionalCharges.create`

Create an additional charge to be invoiced at start of next period: at the end of the current period, the additional charges for a contact are merged where possible and an invoice will be created for them (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.contacts.additionalCharges.create({
	id: '458026356994737217',
	product_id: '440009337465900001',
	amount: '121.00',
	period: '202604',
	description: 'Consulting April',
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `product_id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `amount` | `string \| number` | Yes | The quantity on the invoice line, e.g. `1` or `5 x`. |
| `price` | `string \| number \| null` | No | An amount of money. Both a decimal and a string '10,95' are accepted. A string is bound to the same range as a number, -1,000,000,000 &lt;= *n* &lt;= 1,000,000,000. |
| `period` | `string` | Yes | The period the charge applies to, e.g. `20250101..20250131`, `202501..202503` or `this_month`. |
| `description` | `string` | Yes | — |
| `identifier` | `string` | No | Your own reference for this charge. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `administration_id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `contact_id` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |

### filter

`contacts.filter`

Filter contacts, one page at a time (scopes: any of estimates, sales_invoices, documents, bank or settings)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.contacts.filter({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `first_name:henk,contact_type:company`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| - \| - \| - \| - \| \| created_after \| `String` \| \| Select contacts created after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone \| \| updated_after \| `String` \| \| Select contacts updated after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone \| \| first_name \| `String` \| \| Select contacts with the given first name. Case-insensitive \| \| last_name \| `String` \| \| Select contacts with the given last name. Case-insensitive \| \| estimate_workflow_id \| `Integer` \| \| Filters contacts by a single Estimate workflow \| \| invoice_workflow_id \| `Integer` \| \| Filters contacts by a single Invoice workflow \| \| contact_type \| `String` \| \| The contact type. Possible values `all`, `company`, `private_individual` \| \| delivery_method \| `String` \| \| The delivery method for invoices. Possible values. Possible values `all`, `email`, `post`, `manual`, `peppol`, `simplerinvoicing` \| \| trusted_type \| `String` \| \| Whether the contact is trusted. Possible values `all`, `trusted`, `not_trusted` \| \| mandate_type \| `String` \| \| The direct debit mandate of the contact. Possible values `all`, `manual` (the SEPA mandate fields are filled in), `adyen` (an accepted Moneybird mandate), `none` (no mandate at all) \| |
| `query` | `string` | No | Free-text search across name, contact people, email, phone, customer id, tax number, chamber of commerce, IBAN, and address fields. |
| `include_archived` | `boolean \| string` | No | — |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `attachment_id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

### generalDocuments.list

`documents.generalDocuments.list`

Get general documents, one page at a time (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.generalDocuments.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:open`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| - \| - \| - \| - \| \| period \| `String` \| `this_year` \| A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. \| \| state \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `new`, `saved`, `open`, `paid`, `late` or `pending_payment`. `paid`, `late` and `pending_payment` only apply to documents with a payment lifecycle (purchase invoices and receipts) \| \| recurring \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `enabled` or `disabled` \| \| attachment \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `with` or `without` \| \| reference \| `String` \| \| Documents with the given reference value \| \| contact_id \| `Integer` \| \| Documents belonging to the given contact \| \| ledger_account_id \| `Integer` \| \| Documents booking against the given ledger account \| \| updated_after \| `String` \| \| ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC; documents updated strictly after this time \| Multiple values for `state`, `recurring` and `attachment` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:open\|paid`. |
| `new_filter` | `string` | No | String terms, example: `key1:value1,key2:value2`. |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `sort` | `date_desc \| date_asc` | No | Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first. |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

### generalJournalDocuments.attachments.download

`documents.generalJournalDocuments.attachments.download`

Download attachment: download the attachment (returned as a file) (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.generalJournalDocuments.attachments.download({ id: '458026356994737217', attachment_id: '442001234567000001' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `attachment_id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

### generalJournalDocuments.list

`documents.generalJournalDocuments.list`

Get general journal documents, one page at a time (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.generalJournalDocuments.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:open`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| - \| - \| - \| - \| \| period \| `String` \| `this_year` \| A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. \| \| state \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `new`, `saved`, `open`, `paid`, `late` or `pending_payment`. `paid`, `late` and `pending_payment` only apply to documents with a payment lifecycle (purchase invoices and receipts) \| \| recurring \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `enabled` or `disabled` \| \| attachment \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `with` or `without` \| \| reference \| `String` \| \| Documents with the given reference value \| \| contact_id \| `Integer` \| \| Documents belonging to the given contact \| \| ledger_account_id \| `Integer` \| \| Documents booking against the given ledger account \| \| updated_after \| `String` \| \| ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC; documents updated strictly after this time \| Multiple values for `state`, `recurring` and `attachment` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:open\|paid`. |
| `new_filter` | `string` | No | String terms, example: `key1:value1,key2:value2`. |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `sort` | `date_desc \| date_asc` | No | Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first. |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `exclude_new_general_journal_documents` | `boolean \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

### purchaseInvoices.attachments.download

`documents.purchaseInvoices.attachments.download`

Download attachment: download the attachment (returned as a file) (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.purchaseInvoices.attachments.download({ id: '458026356994737217', attachment_id: '442001234567000001' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `attachment_id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

### purchaseInvoices.list

`documents.purchaseInvoices.list`

Get purchase invoices, one page at a time (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.purchaseInvoices.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:open`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| - \| - \| - \| - \| \| period \| `String` \| `this_year` \| Matches on the document date. A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. \| \| state \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `new`, `saved`, `open`, `paid`, `late` or `pending_payment`. `paid`, `late` and `pending_payment` only apply to documents with a payment lifecycle (purchase invoices and receipts) \| \| recurring \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `enabled` or `disabled` \| \| attachment \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `with` or `without` \| \| automatic_saving \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `automatic` or `manual`. `automatic` matches documents Moneybird saved by itself after analysing them; `manual` matches everything else, including documents nobody has saved yet \| \| reference \| `String` \| \| Documents with the given reference value \| \| contact_id \| `Integer` \| \| Documents belonging to the given contact \| \| ledger_account_id \| `Integer` \| \| Documents booking against the given ledger account \| \| updated_after \| `String` \| \| ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC; documents updated strictly after this time \| The `period` filter matches on the document date. It does not look at the `period` of the individual details, which says which months the expenses belong to. Read `details[].period` in the response when you need those months, or use the reports endpoints, which already spread the amounts over that period. A detail's period can fall outside the filtered range, however wide you make it, so this filter cannot tell you which periods amounts fall in. Use the reports endpoints for that. Multiple values for `state`, `recurring` and `attachment` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:open\|paid`. |
| `new_filter` | `string` | No | String terms, example: `key1:value1,key2:value2`. |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `sort` | `date_desc \| date_asc` | No | Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first. |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

### receipts.attachments.create

`documents.receipts.attachments.create`

Add attachment to receipt: add an attachment to a receipt (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.receipts.attachments.create({
	id: '458026356994737217',
	file: { base64: 'JVBERi0xLjQKJSVFT0YK', filename: 'invoice.pdf', contentType: 'application/pdf' },
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `file` | `string \| object \| custom` | No | A file: a public URL to it, or &#123;url, filename?, contentType?&#125;, or &#123;base64, filename?, contentType?&#125; for a small one. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="file full type">

```ts
string | {
  url: string,
  filename?: string,
  contentType?: string
} | {
  base64: string,
  filename?: string,
  contentType?: string
} | custom
```
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>



**Output:** `number`

### receipts.attachments.delete

`documents.receipts.attachments.delete`

Delete an attachment (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.receipts.attachments.delete({ id: '458026356994737217', attachment_id: '442001234567000001' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `attachment_id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Moneybird accepted the call; it answered with no body. |

### receipts.attachments.download

`documents.receipts.attachments.download`

Download attachment: download the attachment (returned as a file) (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.receipts.attachments.download({ id: '458026356994737217', attachment_id: '442001234567000001' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `attachment_id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

### receipts.list

`documents.receipts.list`

List receipts, one page at a time (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.receipts.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:open`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| - \| - \| - \| - \| \| period \| `String` \| `this_year` \| Matches on the document date. A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. \| \| state \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `new`, `saved`, `open`, `paid`, `late` or `pending_payment`. `paid`, `late` and `pending_payment` only apply to documents with a payment lifecycle (purchase invoices and receipts) \| \| recurring \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `enabled` or `disabled` \| \| attachment \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `with` or `without` \| \| automatic_saving \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `automatic` or `manual`. `automatic` matches documents Moneybird saved by itself after analysing them; `manual` matches everything else, including documents nobody has saved yet \| \| reference \| `String` \| \| Documents with the given reference value \| \| contact_id \| `Integer` \| \| Documents belonging to the given contact \| \| ledger_account_id \| `Integer` \| \| Documents booking against the given ledger account \| \| updated_after \| `String` \| \| ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC; documents updated strictly after this time \| The `period` filter matches on the document date. It does not look at the `period` of the individual details, which says which months the expenses belong to. Read `details[].period` in the response when you need those months, or use the reports endpoints, which already spread the amounts over that period. A detail's period can fall outside the filtered range, however wide you make it, so this filter cannot tell you which periods amounts fall in. Use the reports endpoints for that. Multiple values for `state`, `recurring` and `attachment` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:open\|paid`. |
| `new_filter` | `string` | No | String terms, example: `key1:value1,key2:value2`. |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `sort` | `date_desc \| date_asc` | No | Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first. |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

### typelessDocuments.attachments.download

`documents.typelessDocuments.attachments.download`

Download attachment: download the attachment (returned as a file) (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.typelessDocuments.attachments.download({ id: '458026356994737217', attachment_id: '442001234567000001' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `attachment_id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

### typelessDocuments.list

`documents.typelessDocuments.list`

Get typeless documents, one page at a time (scope: documents)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.documents.typelessDocuments.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:open`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| - \| - \| - \| - \| \| period \| `String` \| `this_year` \| A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. \| \| state \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `new`, `saved`, `open`, `paid`, `late` or `pending_payment`. `paid`, `late` and `pending_payment` only apply to documents with a payment lifecycle (purchase invoices and receipts) \| \| recurring \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `enabled` or `disabled` \| \| attachment \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `with` or `without` \| \| reference \| `String` \| \| Documents with the given reference value \| \| contact_id \| `Integer` \| \| Documents belonging to the given contact \| \| ledger_account_id \| `Integer` \| \| Documents booking against the given ledger account \| \| updated_after \| `String` \| \| ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC; documents updated strictly after this time \| Multiple values for `state`, `recurring` and `attachment` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:open\|paid`. |
| `new_filter` | `string` | No | String terms, example: `key1:value1,key2:value2`. |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |

## Downloads

### download

`downloads.download`

Download a file (returned as a file)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.downloads.download({ id: '458026356994737217' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |



---


| Name | Type | Required | Description |

### downloadPdf

`estimates.downloadPdf`

Download estimate PDF by id: redirects to the download URL of the estimate as PDF (returned as a file) (scope: estimates)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.estimates.downloadPdf({ id: '458026356994737217' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `media` | `string` | No | In case you want to hide sender address and logo you can set this to 'stationery'. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

### list

`estimates.list`

List all estimates, one page at a time (scope: estimates)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.estimates.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:all`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| --- \| --- \| --- \| --- \| \| state \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `draft`, `open`, `late`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `billed` or `archived` \| \| period \| `String` \| `this_year` \| Matches on the estimate date. This can either be the description of a period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom period (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. \| \| contact_id \| `Integer` \| \| Filters estimates by a single contact \| \| workflow_id \| `Integer` \| \| Filters estimates by a single workflow \| The `period` filter matches on the estimate date. It does not look at the `period` of the individual details, which says which months the expenses belong to. Read `details[].period` in the response when you need those months, or use the reports endpoints, which already spread the amounts over that period. A detail's period can fall outside the filtered range, however wide you make it, so this filter cannot tell you which periods amounts fall in. Use the reports endpoints for that. You can filter by multiple states at the same time as well. To do this, separate the state values by a pipe: `state:draft\|scheduled`. |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

### send

`estimates.send`

Send an estimate to the contact (sends real email) or schedule it (scope: estimates)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.estimates.send({
	id: '458026356994737217',
	estimate_sending: { delivery_method: 'Email' },
});
```

### attachments.download

`externalSalesInvoices.attachments.download`

Download attachment: download the attachment (returned as a file) (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.externalSalesInvoices.attachments.download({ external_sales_invoice_id: '458026356994737217', id: '458026356994737217' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `external_sales_invoice_id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

### list

`externalSalesInvoices.list`

List all external invoices, one page at a time (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.externalSalesInvoices.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:all`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| --- \| --- \| --- \| --- \| \| state \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `new`, `open`, `late`, `paid`, or `uncollectible` \| \| period \| `String` \| `this_year` \| Matches on the invoice date. This can either be the description of a period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom period (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. \| \| contact_id \| `Integer` \| \| Select invoices belonging to a certain contact \| The `period` filter matches on the invoice date. It does not look at the `period` of the individual details, which says which months the expenses belong to. Read `details[].period` in the response when you need those months, or use the reports endpoints, which already spread the amounts over that period. A detail's period can fall outside the filtered range, however wide you make it, so this filter cannot tell you which periods amounts fall in. Use the reports endpoints for that. You can filter by multiple states at the same time as well. To do this, separate the state values by a pipe: `state:new\|open`. |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| - \| - \| - \| - \| \| period \| `String` \| `this_year` \| A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. \| \| state \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `unprocessed`, `processed` or `auto_booked` \| \| mutation_type \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `debit` or `credit` \| \| financial_account_id \| `Integer` \| \| Restrict to a single financial account \| \| amount_from \| `String` \| \| Lower bound on the absolute mutation amount (negative input is treated as positive) \| \| amount_to \| `String` \| \| Upper bound on the absolute mutation amount \| Multiple values for `state` and `mutation_type` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:unprocessed\|processed`. |

### download

`purchaseTransactionBatches.download`

Download a purchase transaction batch as SEPA credit transfer file: download the purchase transaction batch as a SEPA credit transfer file (pain.001) (returned as a file) (scope: bank)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.purchaseTransactionBatches.download({ id: '458026356994737217' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `contentBase64` | `string` | No | The file, base64-encoded. Missing when the file came back as text or contentOmitted is set. |
| `text` | `string` | No | The file as text, in place of contentBase64, when it is a text file (CSV, JSON, Markdown, XML and the like) in UTF-8. |
| `contentType` | `string` | Yes | Media type of the file, for example application/pdf. |
| `byteLength` | `number` | Yes | Size of the file in bytes. |
| `filename` | `string` | No | The file name, when known. |
| `contentOmitted` | `not_requested \| over_limit` | No | Set when the content was left out: the caller did not ask for it, or the file was over the limit. |
| `fileId` | `string` | No | Where the host saved the file. Over the limit it comes in place of the content; a host that keeps every file sets it beside the content too. On Corsair it is a Files id (fil_…): pass it to another app wherever that app takes a file URL, or read a text file or PDF with files.read_text. |

### create

`recurringSalesInvoices.create`

Creates a new recurring sales invoice: a recurring sales invoice will create new sales invoices on set intervals (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.recurringSalesInvoices.create({
	recurring_sales_invoice: { update_contact: true },
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `recurring_sales_invoice` | `object` | No | — |

### deactivate

### delete

`recurringSalesInvoices.delete`

Destroy or deactivate a recurring sales invoice: a recurring sales invoice will be destroyed if it has not created any sales invoices (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.recurringSalesInvoices.delete({ id: '458026356994737217' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Moneybird accepted the call; it answered with no body. |

### fetchByIds

`recurringSalesInvoices.fetchByIds`

Fetch recurring sales invoices with given IDs: given a list of recurring sales invoice IDs, returns the details of the recurring invoices (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.recurringSalesInvoices.fetchByIds({
	ids: [1],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `ids` | `(number \| string)[]` | Yes | — |



**Output:** `object[]`

---

### list

`recurringSalesInvoices.list`

List all recurring sales invoices, one page at a time (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.recurringSalesInvoices.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `state:active,contact_id:123`). A filter key you leave out keeps its default below. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| --- \| --- \| --- \| --- \| \| state \| `String` \| `active` \| `active` or `inactive` \| \| frequency \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `quarter` or `year` \| \| auto_send \| `Boolean` \| `null` \| `null`, `true` or `false` \| \| contact_id \| `Integer` \| \| Filters recurring invoices by a single contact \| \| workflow_id \| `Integer` \| \| Filters recurring invoices by a single workflow \| \| include_subscriptions \| `Boolean` \| `false` \| Use `true` to include the recurring sales invoices that belong to a subscription \| |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

### fetchByIds

`salesInvoices.fetchByIds`

Fetch sales invoices with given ids: given a list of sales invoice ids, returns the sales invoice information belonging to the invoices (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.salesInvoices.fetchByIds({
	ids: [1],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `ids` | `(number \| string)[]` | Yes | — |



**Output:** `object[]`

---

### list

`salesInvoices.list`

List sales invoices with a filter string such as 'state:open|paid' or 'period:this_year', one page at a time (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.salesInvoices.list({ filter: 'state:open|late', per_page: 100 });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:all`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| - \| - \| - \| - \| \| state \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `draft`, `open`, `scheduled`, `pending_payment`, `late`, `reminded`, `paid` or `uncollectible` \| \| period \| `String` \| `this_year` \| Matches on the invoice date. A period description (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom period (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. \| \| reference \| `String` \| \| Select invoices with a certain reference \| \| contact_id \| `Integer` \| \| Select invoices belonging to a certain contact \| \| recurring_sales_invoice_id \| `Integer` \| \| Select invoices created by a certain recurring invoice \| \| workflow_id \| `Integer` \| \| Select invoices that use a certain workflow \| \| created_after \| `String` \| \| Select invoices created after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone \| \| updated_after \| `String` \| \| Select invoices updated after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone \| The `period` filter matches on the invoice date. It does not look at the `period` of the individual details, which says which months the expenses belong to. Read `details[].period` in the response when you need those months, or use the reports endpoints, which already spread the amounts over that period. A detail's period can fall outside the filtered range, however wide you make it, so this filter cannot tell you which periods amounts fall in. Use the reports endpoints for that. You can filter by multiple states at the same time by separating the values with a pipe (`state:draft\|scheduled`). This also holds for the reference. A draft with no `invoice_date` set is only matched by a `period` when that period contains today. To list drafts irrespective of date, pass `state:draft` without a `period`; to narrow them down in time, use `created_after` or `updated_after`. |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `sort` | `date_desc \| date_asc` | No | Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first. |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

### resume

`salesInvoices.resume`

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.salesInvoices.resume({ id: '458026356994737217' });
```

### send

`salesInvoices.send`

Send the invoice to the customer now (email, Peppol, post or manual) or schedule it for a date; defaults come from the contact and workflow (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.salesInvoices.send({
	id: '437485325512000001',
```

### sendReminders

`salesInvoices.sendReminders`

Send payment reminders for overdue sales invoices to their contacts (sends real email) (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.salesInvoices.sendReminders({
	sales_invoice_reminders: [{
		contact_id: '387172987357643188',
		workflow_id: '458026356994737217',
		document_style_id: '458026356994737217',
		identity_id: '458026356994737217',
		sales_invoice_ids: ['437485325512000001'],
	}],
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `sales_invoice_reminders` | `object[]` | Yes | — |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="sales_invoice_reminders full type">

```ts
{
  contact_id: string | number,
  workflow_id: string | number,
  document_style_id: string | number,
  identity_id: string | number,
  sales_invoice_ids: (string | number)[],
  reminder_text?: string,
  delivery_method?: Email | Manual,
  email_address?: string
}[]
```

### update

`salesInvoices.update`

Update a sales invoice: when updating a sales invoice, provide only the attributes you want to update (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.salesInvoices.update({
	id: '437485325512000001',
	sales_invoice: { reference: 'PO-42' },
});
```

| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `sales_invoice` | `object` | No | — |

## Subscriptions

### additionalCharges.create

`subscriptions.additionalCharges.create`

Create an additional charge to be invoiced together with the subscription: at the end of the current subscription period, the additional charges are merged where possible and an invoice will be created for them (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.subscriptions.additionalCharges.create({
	id: '458026356994737217',
	product_id: '440009337465900001',
	amount: '121.00',
	period: '202604',
	description: 'Consulting April',
});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `product_id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `amount` | `string \| number` | Yes | The quantity on the invoice line, e.g. `1` or `5 x`. |
| `price` | `string \| number \| null` | No | An amount of money. Both a decimal and a string '10,95' are accepted. A string is bound to the same range as a number, -1,000,000,000 &lt;= *n* &lt;= 1,000,000,000. |
| `period` | `string` | Yes | The period the charge applies to, e.g. `20250101..20250131`, `202501..202503` or `this_month`. |
| `description` | `string` | Yes | — |
| `identifier` | `string` | No | Your own reference for this charge. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `administration_id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `contact_id` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `subscription_id` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `product_id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `detail_id` | `string \| number \| null \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `amount` | `string \| null \| null` | No | — |
| `price` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `period` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `description` | `string \| null` | No | — |

### additionalCharges.list

`subscriptions.additionalCharges.list`

Get additional charges: get the additional charges of the given subscription (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.subscriptions.additionalCharges.list({ id: '458026356994737217' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |
| `include_billed` | `boolean \| string` | No | If true, includes the additional charges that have already been billed. Default is false. |

`subscriptions.create`

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.subscriptions.create({
	subscription: { start_date: '2026-04-09', product_id: '440009337465900001', contact_id: '387172987357643188' },
});
```

### createAndScheduleOneOffSalesInvoice

`subscriptions.createAndScheduleOneOffSalesInvoice`

Create and schedule an invoice to be sent together with the subscription: besides the recurring sales invoice for the subscription, you sometimes need to bill separate costs like usage based charges (scope: sales_invoices)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.subscriptions.createAndScheduleOneOffSalesInvoice({
	id: '458026356994737217',

});
```

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.taskLists.delete({ id: '458026356994737217' });
```

| Name | Type | Required | Description |

**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Moneybird accepted the call; it answered with no body. |

## Tax Rates

### list

`taxRates.list`

List all available tax rates for the administration, one page at a time (scopes: any of settings, sales_invoices, documents or estimates)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.taxRates.list({});
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `percentage:21,tax_rate_type:sales_invoice`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| --- \| --- \| --- \| --- \| \| name \| `String` \| \| Select tax rates by their full name \| \| partial_name \| `String` \| \| Select tax rates with this substring in their name \| \| percentage \| `Integer` \| \| Select tax rates with the specified percentage, e.g. specify `21` for 21% \| \| tax_rate_type \| `String` \| \| `general_journal_document`, `purchase_invoice` or `sales_invoice`. Without this filter, tax rates of all types are returned \| \| country \| `String` \| \| Select tax rates with the specified country. Must be a 2 letter abbreviation following ISO 3166. Please note that only foreign tax rates will have this field set. Domestic tax rates will not have this set at the moment. \| \| show_tax \| `Boolean` \| \| Use `true` to tax rates for which tax is shown on the invoice, `false` for when it's not shown. No value will select both \| \| active \| `Boolean` \| \| Use `true` to select active tax rates. Use `false` for inactive tax rates. No value will select both \| \| created_after \| `String` \| \| Tax rates created after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone \| \| updated_after \| `String` \| \| Tax rates updated after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone \| You can filter by multiple tax rate types at the same time by separating the values with a pipe (`tax_rate_type:purchase_invoice\|sales_invoice`). |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="items full type">

```ts

  id?: string | number | null,
  administration_id?: string | number | null,
  name?: string | null,
  percentage?: string | number | null | null | null,
  tax_rate_type?: string | null,
  show_tax?: boolean | null | null,
  active?: boolean | null | null,
  country?: string | null | null,
  created_at?: string | null | null,
  updated_at?: string | null | null
}[]
```

### delete

`timeEntries.delete`

Delete a time entry: delete a time entry by id (scope: time_entries)

**Risk:** `destructive` · **Irreversible**

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.timeEntries.delete({ id: '458026356994737217' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `success` | `true` | Yes | Moneybird accepted the call; it answered with no body. |

### list

`timeEntries.list`

List all time entries, one page at a time (scope: time_entries)

**Risk:** `read`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.timeEntries.list({ filter: 'period:this_year' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `filter` | `string` | No | Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:all`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: \| **Filter** \| **Type** \| **Default** \| **Description** \| \| --- \| --- \| --- \| --- \| \| state \| `String` \| `all` \| `all`, `open` or `non_billable` \| \| period \| `String` \| `this_year` \| This can either be the description of a period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom period (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. \| \| contact_id \| `Integer` \| \| Select time entries belonging to a certain contact \| \| include_nil_contacts \| `Boolean` \| false \| Whether to include time entries that have no assigned contact \| \| include_active \| `Boolean` \| false \| Whether to include active time entries i.e. time entries without ended_at \| \| project_id \| `Integer` \| \| Select time entries belonging to a certain project \| \| user_id \| `Integer` \| \| Select time entries belonging to a certain user \| \| day \| `Date` \| \| Select time entries on a specific date \| You can filter by multiple states at the same time as well. To do this, separate the state values by a pipe: `state:open\|non_billable`. |
| `page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `per_page` | `number \| string` | No | — |
| `query` | `string` | No | Free-text search across the time entry description. |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `items` | `object[]` | Yes | One page of results. |
| `next_page` | `number \| null` | Yes | The page to ask for next: set while this page came back full (per_page; 100 when left out), null once it came back short. |

**Risk:** `write`

```ts

	time_entry_id: '458026356994737217',

});
```

## Webhooks

### activate

`webhooks.activate`

Activate a webhook: activates a previously deactivated webhook (scope: settings)

**Risk:** `write`

```ts
await corsair.moneybird.api.webhooks.activate({ id: '458026356994737217' });
```

**Input**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `administration_id` | `string \| number` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `id` | `string \| number` | Yes | A unique record identifier |



**Output**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|------|------|----------|-------------|
| `id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `administration_id` | `string \| number \| null` | No | A unique record identifier |
| `url` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `enabled_events` | `string[] \| null` | No | List of events this webhook is subscribed to. See [webhook events](https://developer.moneybird.com/webhooks/events) for all available events and event groups. |
| `last_http_status` | `number \| string \| null \| null` | No | HTTP status code of the request last received back from the webhook |
| `last_http_body` | `string \| null \| null` | No | Body of the request last received back from the webhook |
| `token` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `secret` | `string \| null` | No | The webhook's secret, used to generate webhook signatures. Only returned at creation. |
| `deactivated_at` | `string \| null \| null` | No | Timestamp when the webhook was deactivated. Null if the webhook is active. |

| `url` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `enabled_events` | `string[] \| null` | No | List of events this webhook is subscribed to. See [webhook events](https://developer.moneybird.com/webhooks/events) for all available events and event groups. |
| `last_http_status` | `number \| string \| null \| null` | No | HTTP status code of the request last received back from the webhook |
| `last_http_body` | `string \| null \| null` | No | Body of the request last received back from the webhook |
| `token` | `string \| null` | No | — |
| `secret` | `string \| null` | No | The webhook's secret, used to generate webhook signatures. Only returned at creation. |
